title: Break it into stories
do: In Home, type /, pick Iterate on something, type: Break the Visma connector into stories under SCH-118. Rebecca's team, after Fortnox, Fjord Sports first. Round one: Keep it on the first three, Cut it on the pilot, skip Anything else. Round two: keep all three.
offScript: That is outside what this demo can show. The five things it can do are listed in Settings, under Demo.

text: Deciding: the stories that make up the Visma connector under SCH-118, for Rebecca's team once the Fortnox connector is done ([[decisions/2026-05-20-fortnox-first-payroll-target]]).
Out of scope: a date, and anything that needs the token store before PLT-77 lands ([[tickets/jira/PLT-77]]).
Done looks like: three or four stories you would file as they stand, three acceptance checkboxes each, Fjord Sports named where they are the reason ([[customers/fjord-sports]]).
Four ideas. Keep or cut each one.

questions.question: Connect a customer's Visma account through the PLT-77 token store.
questions.body:
The case: Fortnox already goes through the token store, and Nils refused to keep refresh tokens anywhere else ([[tickets/jira/SCH-125]]). Visma is the second integration the store was built for ([[tickets/jira/PLT-77]]), so this story is the connect screen, the consent flow and the per-tenant token, nothing new underneath.

The cost: it cannot start until refresh-on-expiry lands in PLT-77, and it is the story every other Visma story waits on. If PLT-77 slips, this slips with it.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: One story: connect a Visma account, tokens in the platform store.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: Then the connector has nowhere to keep credentials, and the push story has to invent one.

questions.question: Reuse the SCH-125 cost-centre mapping for Visma.
questions.body:
The case: Fortnox maps each location to a cost centre, and the CSV already uses one column set both systems accept ([[tickets/jira/SCH-121]]). Visma needs the same mapping with Visma's own identifiers. Reusing the screen and the model keeps this to a week of adapter work rather than a second mapping feature.

The cost: the Fortnox mapping is built for Fortnox's identifiers. If Visma's cost-centre model differs (Fjord Sports run 60 stores under regional cost centres), the reuse turns into a refactor of SCH-125 that lands on the Fortnox team's plate first.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: One story: map locations to Visma cost centres on the existing screen.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: Then Visma gets its own mapping story, written from scratch.

questions.question: One push per pay period, with a report of what Visma rejected.
questions.body:
The case: this is the story Oskar is waiting for. Approved hours go from the period view straight into Visma, one push per pay period per store, and the manager reads a plain report of anything Visma refused ([[meetings/2026-05-26-fjord-sports-payroll-call]]). Same shape as the Fortnox push in SCH-125.

The cost: the rejection report is the half of the work nobody scopes. Visma's error responses are not Fortnox's, and a report a manager can act on takes longer than the push itself.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: One story: push per pay period plus the rejection report, together.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: Then the connector connects and maps but never sends, and the file stays the product.

questions.question: Run the first push with Fjord Sports' 60 stores before it goes to every chain.
questions.body:
The case: Fjord Sports asked first, planned their migration around it, and have a regional admin who does the retyping today ([[insights/fjord-sports-expects-payroll-q4]]). A pilot with them finds the cost-centre and rejection cases before any other chain sees them.

The cost: a pilot is a project, not a story. It needs a feature flag per chain, someone from CS in the loop for the first two pay periods, and a date we do not have. Under an epic it becomes the story that never closes.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: One story: a per-chain flag and a pilot checklist for Fjord Sports.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: Fjord Sports stays in the first line of the other stories; the pilot is a rollout decision, not a ticket.

questions.question: What is missing, what should merge, what did I get wrong?

text: Three kept, the pilot cut. Fjord Sports stays in the first line of each story instead.
Next level down: the same three as stories, each with its three checks. Keep or cut.

questions.question: Connect a customer's Visma account through the token store.
questions.body:
Fjord Sports first: their regional admin connects one Visma account for the chain.

Acceptance:
- A chain admin connects a Visma account from the payroll settings screen and sees it as connected.
- Refresh tokens live in the platform token store (PLT-77), per tenant, never in the scheduling service.
- Disconnecting removes the token and stops every push for that chain.

questions.question: Map locations to Visma cost centres, reusing the Fortnox mapping.
questions.body:
Fjord Sports first: 60 stores, mapped once by head office.

Acceptance:
- The mapping screen from SCH-125 lists every location with a Visma cost centre to fill in.
- A location with no cost centre is flagged before the first push, not rejected after it.
- Changing a mapping applies to the next pay period only, never to hours already pushed.

questions.question: Push approved hours to Visma once per pay period, with a rejection report.
questions.body:
Fjord Sports first: approved hours per store leave the period view and land in Visma, so the regional admin stops retyping.

Acceptance:
- A manager pushes one pay period for one store from the period view, and the push cannot be repeated for the same period without confirming.
- Every line Visma rejects comes back as a report naming the person, the date and the reason, in plain words.
- A pushed period is marked in the period view with the time it was sent.

questions.question: Anything to change before they become tickets?

turns.text: Three cards, one per story, under SCH-118 in the team's shape: one label, Fjord Sports in the first line, three checks each. The reasoning stays in this session.

text: Three story cards wait under SCH-118: connect, map, push. Approve the ones you want and they land in Jira with the label and the three checks. The pilot is a rollout decision, so it is not a ticket; Fjord Sports is in the first line of each story instead.
No date on any of them. Visma cannot start before PLT-77 lands, and the Fortnox connector goes first.
